as_told.title: Nixon passed US UFO knowledge to the Soviet Union

plain: The story goes that in the early 1970s, at a summit between the US and the Soviet Union, President Richard Nixon opened a small folder and showed it to the Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev. Yuri Andropov, then head of the Soviet secret police, was in the room. In the story's telling, what Nixon shared was about UFOs, and the American flights to the moon came to an end around that time. The fullest version comes from Kiran Ilum Xenov, the former president of a Russian republic, who tells Michels he heard it from Mikhail Gorbachev, the later Soviet leader. Xenov describes the folder with his hands: 'a small folder like this that he opened and showed to Brev,' with 'Andropov … present at that meeting.' Michels repeats the story back to him in his own words. In his version Nixon gave the Soviets 'information … about what the CIA and the White House knew about UFOs and aliens,' and he says nothing of the folder or the moon flights. If it were true, the two Cold War rivals would have quietly shared their UFO secrets at the highest level.
